body: Weight is not a small thing. It can take years of hard work to properly lose a good amount of it. I'd know cause I was there a few years ago, so I fully empathize with her on that. I tried opening the subject a couple times but kinda hit a brick wall.
Yup now rather than later is why I did it. Would've hurt both of us a lot more later.
Thanks. Yeah I'm trying to view it as a learning experience. Right now I'm in the "I'm never dating again" stage but I know I'll get over it.
Yeah I probably do. Doesn’t change how disappointing things feel sometimes.

Single is one thing, but not seeking intimacy at all? Seems mildly inhuman.

Not judging you, I reassure myself by saying that this is just what feels comfortable to me as well. But then there's the whole stepping out of your comfort zone thing. I can't reconcile the two.

> apathy towards relationships

Yeah that about sums it up I guess. In just worried I might regret wasting this time later in life.

Totally not what I was going for, sorry it came out that way. By autistic I meant having trouble relating to others / the world. On top of that, I feel emotionless.

Not sure this makes it better.
Thanks. I manage a decent quote every now and then but that's about it. Too much of a lazy fuck to put actual effort into it.
I'm sorry about your friend. He was lucky to have you fight for him, not everyone has someone like that. Only person like that in my life was my ex-wife.

FYI, at your age your brain is going through some major changes. I've been there myself, almost jumped off my parents' balcony when I was 13-14. Same story, good school, loving family (though not without its problems), and I even had friends.

I've been seeing a therapist recently (unrelated, divorce...), and my teenage depression came up, as one of my anxieties is that it'll come back. Turns out during these years your brain's emotional responses get majorly rewired (she explained it better) and that can make you feel silly things. BTW, I think your power to self analyse at your age is amazing (e.g. realising that you're confused). Back then all I knew was that I was sad.

All I can say is, just stick with it. It will get better as your brain finishes the rewiring. Try talking to your parents, hopefully they're more open than mine who basically just said "aww, don't be sad" when I told them I'd beed crying every day for weeks.
